title: runKernelBench
responsibility: Runs the kernel benchmark, derives the default and records the run.

inputs.name: runKernelBench.options
inputs.description: The required options object supplies the CLI command prefix and can select a repository root, sample plan, and optional write. The root defaults to process.cwd(); omitted quick remains undefined and selects 3 workloads with 9 cold samples and 200 warm iterations, while true selects the first 2 workloads with 3 and 30; omitted write remains undefined and skips saving, while a truthy value writes through MeasurementRepository.

inputs.name: renderBench.benchmark
inputs.description: A KernelBenchmark object whose workloads, measurements, default, profile, source state, and provenance are read to form the report. Missing or null matching metric values render as n/a.

provenance.note: Observational measurements from a local benchmark run. They are not verification evidence and cannot establish or satisfy a budget baseline.

measurements.method: Median of 3 fresh-process samples: create the runtime, serialize the request, invoke once and parse the response. CLI startup is excluded because every runtime pays it.

default.rule: Lowest median cold end-to-end latency on the representative workload for this profile; within 5% the simpler runtime wins (module, then wasm, then process). Unmeasured or unavailable runtimes are never chosen.

excluded.reason: Needs an independently served unit; never chosen automatically.

outputs.name: runKernelBench
outputs.description: Resolves to calibration data containing the impact-kernel contract, source state, machine profile, workloads, measurements, provenance, and selected default runtime. Quick mode uses the first two fixed workload sizes and the full plan uses all three; writing occurs only when write is truthy.

outputs.name: renderBench
outputs.description: A multiline text report with one row per workload and runtime, followed by the chosen default and calibration provenance. Missing or null metric values render as n/a.
examples:
Impact kernel benchmark on Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8370C CPU @ 2.80GHz (bun 1.3.1).
  graph-100  module   cold 0.120 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-100  wasm     cold 0.160 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-100  process  cold 0.200 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-100  http     cold 0.180 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-1k   module   cold 1.200 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-1k   wasm     cold 1.250 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-1k   process  cold 1.500 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
  graph-1k   http     cold 1.100 ms  warm n/a ms  n/a ops/s
Default: module (measured on graph-1k). Lowest median cold end-to-end latency on the representative workload for this profile; within 5% the simpler runtime wins (module, then wasm, then process). Unmeasured or unavailable runtimes are never chosen.
Provenance: calibration from a clean tree; not verification evidence or a budget baseline.

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Raised when the built kernel artifacts required for benchmarking are unavailable or a cold-sample CLI exits with a nonzero status.

errors.name: Kernel benchmark child startup or readiness failure
errors.description: serveKernel rejects with Error when its child process errors, exits before readiness, exceeds the startup timeout, or returns invalid readiness JSON.
